text: Compare ROSE with TQUG: R, 18, to T, 20 is plus 2. O, 15, to Q, 17 is plus 2. S, 19, to U, 21 is plus 2. E, 5, to G, 7 is plus 2. The rule is: move each letter two steps forward. Apply it to LILY. L becomes N, I becomes K, and the second L becomes N. Now the last letter, Y. Its position is 25, and 25 plus 2 is 27. That is beyond Z, so subtract 26 to get position 1, which is A. LILY is coded as NKNA. If you wrote something odd for the last letter, you've just met the wrap-around trap. It's better to meet it here than in the exam.
